title: The Photograph

evidence.name: Tub of Plastic Wood
evidence.text: In the reeds by the jetty: a lidless tub of plastic wood with a thumbprint in it, and a snapped bit of brass wire. The famous 1934 photograph was a toy submarine with a sculpted head. Same trick, newer tub.

evidence.name: Wee Ripples
evidence.text: The old boatman reads the photograph's ripples like small print. They are the wake of something a foot long, not forty. 'A big beast makes a big fuss. This made a wee one.'

evidence.name: Postcard Stock
evidence.text: The photograph is printed on glossy cream stock with a scalloped edge: exactly the postcards sold from one stall in Inverness.

evidence.name: Till Roll
evidence.text: The ironmonger's till roll: plastic wood, brass wire and a tin of grey paint, bought on one day by 'G. Mackie, cash'. Receipts are the detective's friend and the faker's regret.

evidence.name: Hunter's Notebook
evidence.text: Page after page of drawn necks, dated and numbered, with notes like 'definitely a log, but what a log'. He is earnest, not crafty. The man cannot fold a map.

evidence.name: Boatman's Box Camera
evidence.text: An old box camera in the boatman's cabin, wrong film for the photograph. Also full of spiders. Nobody has taken a picture with it since the 1970s.

suspects.name: The Monster Hunter
suspects.wrong: Fake it? I've spent thirty years hoping it was real! If I'd made a fake, I'd have made a better one. Not that I'm saying I could. Don't write that down.

suspects.name: The Old Boatman
suspects.wrong: I've sailed this loch since before you could walk and never needed a trick. The monster's real enough when the tourists book. I'll thank you to keep your fingers off my tiller.

suspects.name: Gillian Mackie
suspects.right: Alright, you've got me. Plastic wood, a toy boat from a car boot sale and a very good neck. The mugs were going to be gorgeous. Could I still sell it as 'The Famous Fake'? People love a fake. I'll refund every mug.

steps.text: Speak to Ailsa Munro, the archivist, at Loch Ness.
Search the reeds by the jetty at Loch Ness for the photographer's props.
Show the photograph to the old boatman at Loch Ness.
Ask the Monster Hunter at Loch Ness.
Look at the postcard rack on the Inverness market stalls.
Ask the ironmonger in Inverness about the plastic wood.
Have a word with Gillian Mackie on her Inverness stall.
Report back to Ailsa Munro at Loch Ness.

accuse_hint: Ailsa Munro is waiting at Loch Ness.
closed: The mugs have been withdrawn. The Famous Fake now has its own display case, which is the best fate a fake can hope for.
